Two things change with age, and they are hard to separate. Children's
arrangements come to resemble adults' more closely, and children also become
more consistent with themselves. A child who places pictures inconsistently
cannot match the adult arrangement however well they understand the concepts,
so some of the first change follows from the second. This file reports both,
and reports how much of the first the second can account for.

```{r}
#| label: setup
source(here::here("setup.R"))
library(lmerTest); library(broom); library(broom.mixed); library(emmeans)
library(mgcv)                       # linearity check only
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

S <- readRDS("analysis_sample.rds")
fp <- S$children
```

```{r}
#| label: measures
#   consistency  the child's two arrangements against each other
#   similarity   their average arrangement against the adult average
refs <- set_names(S$adult_ref$ref, S$adult_ref$category)
ref_concepts <- set_names(S$adult_ref$concepts, S$adult_ref$category)

child_pdv <- participant_dist_vecs(fp) %>%
  mutate(category = as.character(category))

# Equal vector lengths is not enough: two different sets of twelve concepts
# would correlate the wrong pairs without erroring. Compare the names.
alignment <- child_pdv %>%
  filter(category %in% names(ref_concepts)) %>%
  distinct(category, concepts) %>%
  mutate(matches_adults = map2_lgl(concepts, category,
                                   ~ identical(.x, ref_concepts[[.y]])),
         n_concepts = lengths(concepts)) %>%
  select(category, n_concepts, matches_adults)

show_all(alignment)
stopifnot(nrow(alignment) > 0, all(alignment$matches_adults))

similarity <- child_pdv %>%
  filter(category %in% names(refs)) %>%
  mutate(similarity = map2_dbl(dvec, category,
                               ~ cor(.x, refs[[.y]], method = "spearman"))) %>%
  select(participant_id, category, similarity)

d <- S$consistency %>%
  mutate(category = as.character(category)) %>%
  select(participant_id, category, consistency) %>%
  inner_join(similarity, by = c("participant_id", "category")) %>%
  inner_join(S$age, by = "participant_id") %>%
  add_age_bins() %>%
  mutate(category = fct_domain(category))

tibble(n_children = n_distinct(d$participant_id), n_child_domains = nrow(d)) %>%
  show_all()
```

The methods figure, built from one real child rather than drawn by hand. It
stops where the measures start: an arrangement, the matrix it produces, and
the two matrices compared. Replacing arrangement 2 with the adult average is
the only difference between consistency and similarity.

```{r}
#| label: pipeline-candidates
library(grid)   # base R; avoids a patchwork / ggrepel dependency

DOM <- "animals"

# What makes a good illustration, in order of importance:
#   consistency  close to what children typically show, so panel 3 is honest
#   similarity   the grouping is recognisable, so panel 1 reads as structure
#   gap_ratio    closest pair relative to overall spread; small values mean
#                two pictures sit on top of each other and their labels collide
geom_stats <- fp %>%
  filter(category == DOM) %>%
  group_by(participant_id, trial) %>%
  summarise(spread = mean(dist(cbind(posX, posY))),
            min_gap = min(dist(cbind(posX, posY))), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  slice_min(trial, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(participant_id, spread, min_gap)

# The figure should show what the measure usually looks like, not its best
# case. TARGET is the consistency the example child should have; NULL uses
# the mean for this domain across all children.
PIPELINE_TARGET <- NULL
target_r <- if (!is.null(PIPELINE_TARGET)) PIPELINE_TARGET else
  mean(d$consistency[d$category == DOM], na.rm = TRUE)
cat("typical consistency in", DOM, ":", round(target_r, 3), "\n")

candidates <- d %>%
  filter(category == DOM, !is.na(consistency)) %>%
  select(participant_id, age, similarity, consistency) %>%
  inner_join(geom_stats, by = "participant_id") %>%
  mutate(gap_ratio = min_gap / spread,
         off_target = abs(consistency - target_r))

# Closest to typical first. Pin any of these with PIPELINE_ID below.
candidates %>%
  mutate(across(c(similarity, consistency, gap_ratio, off_target),
                ~ round(.x, 3)),
         spread = round(spread)) %>%
  select(-min_gap) %>%
  arrange(off_target) %>%
  head(15) %>%
  show_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pipeline
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 5.4
# Set this to a participant_id from the table above to pin the figure.
# NULL takes the child whose consistency is closest to the typical value,
# among those with pictures far enough apart that the labels do not overlap.
PIPELINE_ID <- NULL

pick <- if (!is.null(PIPELINE_ID)) PIPELINE_ID else {
  candidates %>%
    filter(gap_ratio > 0.10) %>%
    slice_min(off_target, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    pull(participant_id)
}
stopifnot(length(pick) == 1)
cat("pipeline figure uses participant:", pick, "\n")

board <- filter(fp, participant_id == pick, category == DOM)
tr <- sort(unique(board$trial))
# A methods figure illustrates the procedure, not a domain, so it uses one
# fixed blue rather than borrowing a colour from PALETTE.
HUE <- "#2E6F8E"

bare <- theme_poster(base_size = 20) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = rel(1.2), face = "bold",
                                     colour = "grey10",
                                     margin = margin(b = 8)))

# Labels are pushed radially outward from the centre of the board, so two
# pictures sitting side by side get their names thrown in different
# directions instead of on top of each other.
b1 <- board %>%
  filter(trial == tr[1]) %>%
  mutate(ang = atan2(posY - mean(posY), posX - mean(posX)),
         pad = 0.085 * max(diff(range(posX)), diff(range(posY))),
         lx = posX + cos(ang) * pad,
         ly = posY + sin(ang) * pad,
         hj = 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(ang),
         vj = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(ang))

p_board <- ggplot(b1, aes(posX, posY)) +
  geom_point(size = 5.5, colour = HUE, alpha = .9) +
  geom_text(aes(lx, ly, label = base_name, hjust = hj, vjust = vj),
            size = 5.0, colour = "grey25") +
  scale_y_reverse(expand = expansion(mult = .16)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = .16)) +
  coord_equal(clip = "off") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  bare +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.line = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(6, 22, 6, 22),
        panel.border = element_rect(colour = "grey75", fill = NA))

cd <- trial_concept_dists(filter(board, trial == tr[1]))
p_mat <- as.matrix(as_dist_vec(cd$between, cd$concepts)) %>%
  as.table() %>% as.data.frame(stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  setNames(c("a", "b", "dist")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(a, b, fill = dist)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = .4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = HUE, name = NULL) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  bare +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 55, hjust = 1, size = rel(.8)),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = rel(.8)),
        axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")

v1 <- trial_concept_dists(filter(board, trial == tr[1]))$between
v2 <- trial_concept_dists(filter(board, trial == tr[2]))$between
p_cor <- tibble(t1 = v1, t2 = v2) %>%
  ggplot(aes(t1, t2)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 4.2, alpha = .65, colour = HUE) +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.06, vjust = 1.5,
           label = paste0("r = ", sprintf("%.2f",
                          cor(v1, v2, method = "spearman"))),
           size = 8, fontface = "bold", colour = "grey10") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(.05, .16))) +
  labs(x = "distance, arrangement 1", y = "distance, arrangement 2") +
  bare

# Panel titles are drawn in their own row above the plots, not as ggplot
# subtitles, so all three sit on the same line. (As subtitles they followed
# each plot's own panel, and the square panels pushed them to different
# heights.)
PIPELINE_TITLES <- c("One arrangement",
                     "Pairwise distance matrix",
                     "Within-participant correlation\nfor two arrangements")
PIPELINE_TITLE_SIZE <- 22   # points

draw_pipeline <- function() {
  grid.newpage()
  # Title row height follows the font size and the longest title's number
  # of lines, so a two-line title never runs into the plot below it.
  n_lines <- max(lengths(strsplit(PIPELINE_TITLES, "\n")))
  title_h <- n_lines * PIPELINE_TITLE_SIZE * 1.15 + PIPELINE_TITLE_SIZE
  pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(
    2, 3, heights = unit(c(title_h, 1), c("points", "null")))))
  for (i in 1:3) {
    pushViewport(viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = i))
    grid.text(PIPELINE_TITLES[i],
              y = unit(1, "npc") - unit(PIPELINE_TITLE_SIZE * .4, "points"),
              vjust = 1, gp = gpar(fontsize = PIPELINE_TITLE_SIZE,
                                   fontface = "bold", col = "grey10",
                                   lineheight = .95))
    popViewport()
  }
  print(p_board, vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = 2, layout.pos.col = 1))
  print(p_mat,   vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = 2, layout.pos.col = 2))
  print(p_cor,   vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = 2, layout.pos.col = 3))
  popViewport()
}
draw_pipeline()
```


# Do children do the task consistently?

```{r}
#| label: consistency
# Two-sided: a reliably negative value would mean something is wrong.
d %>%
  filter(!is.na(consistency)) %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(tt = list(t.test(consistency, mu = 0)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(n = map_int(tt, ~ .x$parameter + 1L),
         mean_r = round(map_dbl(tt, ~ unname(.x$estimate)), 3),
         t = round(map_dbl(tt, ~ unname(.x$statistic)), 2),
         p = signif(map_dbl(tt, "p.value"), 3)) %>%
  select(-tt) %>% show_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: consistency-age
lmer(consistency ~ age_c + (1 | participant_id) + (1 | category),
     data = filter(d, !is.na(consistency))) %>%
  # Wald rather than profile likelihood: same answer here, far faster.
  tidy(effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE, conf.method = "Wald") %>%
  select(term, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, statistic, df, p.value) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>% show_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: consistency-table
d %>%
  filter(!is.na(consistency)) %>%
  group_by(age_bin) %>%
  summarise(n_children = n_distinct(participant_id),
            mean_consistency = mean(consistency),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ceiling = ceiling_from(mean_consistency),
         across(c(mean_consistency, ceiling), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  show_all()
```

Consistency rises steeply between four and six and then levels off. The
ceiling column is the highest correlation with the adult arrangement a child
of that consistency could reach. It rises much less steeply than consistency
itself, because the relationship is concave: doubling a low reliability moves
the ceiling a long way, doubling an already decent one barely moves it.

# Do children's arrangements come to resemble adults'?

```{r}
#| label: similarity-age
lmer(similarity ~ age_c + (1 | participant_id) + (1 | category), data = d) %>%
  # Wald rather than profile likelihood: same answer here, far faster.
  tidy(effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE, conf.method = "Wald") %>%
  select(term, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, statistic, df, p.value) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>% show_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: similarity-table
cells <- d %>%
  group_by(category, age_bin) %>%
  # con_se before the means: a new `consistency` column is visible to every
  # argument after it, so sd() would see the mean rather than the column.
  summarise(n_sim = sum(!is.na(similarity)),
            n_con = sum(!is.na(consistency)),
            con_se = sd(consistency, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(consistency))),
            similarity = mean(similarity, na.rm = TRUE),
            consistency = mean(consistency, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_sim >= MIN_BIN_N) %>%
  # sqrt(Spearman-Brown) has infinite slope at zero, so a cell whose
  # reliability is indistinguishable from zero has no usable ceiling.
  mutate(
    reliable = consistency > 2 * con_se,
    ceiling = if_else(reliable, ceiling_from(consistency), NA_real_),
    pct_of_ceiling = 100 * similarity / ceiling,
    category = fct_domain(category))

# Cells with no measurable reliability.
unreliable <- cells %>% filter(!reliable) %>%
  select(category, age_bin, n_con, similarity, consistency, con_se)

if (nrow(unreliable)) show_all(unreliable) else
  cat("Every cell has reliability distinguishable from zero.\n")

cells %>%
  select(category, age_bin, n = n_sim, similarity, consistency,
         ceiling, pct_of_ceiling) %>%
  mutate(across(c(similarity, consistency, ceiling), ~ round(.x, 3)),
         pct_of_ceiling = round(pct_of_ceiling, 1)) %>%
  arrange(category, age_bin) %>% show_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: consistency-domains
# The pooled model averages a steep rise in the object domains with a flat
# line in emotions.
c_dat <- filter(d, !is.na(consistency))
mc_add <- lmer(consistency ~ age_c + category + (1 | participant_id),
               c_dat, REML = FALSE)
mc_int <- lmer(consistency ~ age_c * category + (1 | participant_id),
               c_dat, REML = FALSE)

anova(mc_add, mc_int)

em_con <- emtrends(mc_int, ~ category, var = "age_c")
as_tibble(em_con) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) %>% show_all()

# Pairwise slope differences, unadjusted (see the domains chunk).
as_tibble(pairs(em_con, adjust = "none")) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>% show_all()

contrast(em_con, list(emotions_vs_objects = c(-.5, -.5, 1))) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>% show_all()
```

# How much of that is consistency?

The direct version of the question: does the age effect survive holding
consistency fixed? Both models are fitted on the same rows, since adding
consistency as a predictor drops the children who have no consistency score
and would otherwise shrink the sample as well as change the model.

Consistency is part of what develops, not a nuisance variable, so this is a
robustness check and not the model to report as the main result. If age
survives it, the rise in similarity is not merely children becoming easier to
measure.

```{r}
#| label: control-consistency
cc <- filter(d, !is.na(consistency), !is.na(similarity))

cat("children x domains:", nrow(cc), " similarity-consistency r =",
    round(cor(cc$similarity, cc$consistency, method = "spearman"), 3), "\n\n")

m_base <- lmer(similarity ~ age_c + (1 | participant_id) + (1 | category), cc)
m_ctrl <- lmer(similarity ~ age_c + consistency +
                 (1 | participant_id) + (1 | category), cc)

bind_rows(
  tidy(m_base, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE, conf.method = "Wald") %>%
    mutate(model = "age only"),
  tidy(m_ctrl, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE, conf.method = "Wald") %>%
    mutate(model = "age + consistency")) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  select(model, term, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high,
         statistic, df, p.value) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>% show_all()
```

# Does it differ by domain?

```{r}
#| label: domains
m_add <- lmer(similarity ~ age_c + category + (1 | participant_id),
              data = d, REML = FALSE)
m_int <- lmer(similarity ~ age_c * category + (1 | participant_id),
              data = d, REML = FALSE)

anova(m_add, m_int)

em_sim <- emtrends(m_int, ~ category, var = "age_c")
as_tibble(em_sim) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) %>% show_all()

# Each domain's slope against each other's. Unadjusted, so the emotions rows
# test the same thing as the emotions x animals and emotions x plants
# interaction terms of m_int.
as_tibble(pairs(em_sim, adjust = "none")) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>% show_all()

# The planned contrast: emotions against the mean of animals and plants, one
# test instead of three. Weights follow the domain order animals, plants,
# emotions.
contrast(em_sim, list(emotions_vs_objects = c(-.5, -.5, 1))) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>% show_all()

# Change across the full age range, from the unrounded cell means. `cells`
# stores full precision; only its printed copy is rounded, so subtracting the
# displayed values can land on a rounding boundary.
cells %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(age_from = min(age_bin), age_to = max(age_bin),
            sim_from = similarity[which.min(age_bin)],
            sim_to   = similarity[which.max(age_bin)],
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(change = round(sim_to - sim_from, 3),
         across(c(sim_from, sim_to), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  show_all()
```

The earlier analysis of this dataset used Pearson correlations and reported an
age x domain interaction. This pipeline uses Spearman throughout and does not.
Fitting both on the same children separates the method change from the extra
participants.

```{r}
#| label: pearson-check
sim_both <- child_pdv %>%
  filter(category %in% names(refs)) %>%
  mutate(spearman = map2_dbl(dvec, category,
                             ~ cor(.x, refs[[.y]], method = "spearman")),
         pearson  = map2_dbl(dvec, category,
                             ~ cor(.x, refs[[.y]], method = "pearson"))) %>%
  select(participant_id, category, spearman, pearson) %>%
  inner_join(S$age, by = "participant_id") %>%
  add_age_bins() %>%
  mutate(category = fct_domain(category))

cat("agreement between the two measures: r =",
    round(cor(sim_both$spearman, sim_both$pearson), 3), "\n")

fit_pair <- function(dd, yname) {
  dd <- mutate(dd, y = .data[[yname]])
  m_a <- lmer(y ~ age_c + category + (1 | participant_id), dd, REML = FALSE)
  m_i <- lmer(y ~ age_c * category + (1 | participant_id), dd, REML = FALSE)
  cat("\n---", yname, "---\n")
  print(anova(m_a, m_i))
  as_tibble(emtrends(m_i, ~ category, var = "age_c")) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) %>% show_all()
}

walk(c("spearman", "pearson"), ~ fit_pair(sim_both, .x))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-development
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.2
# One panel per domain: by-age means (+/- 1 SE) over that domain's linear
# fit. facet = FALSE puts all three in one graph. The per-child scatter is gone: plot_by_age(..., raw = TRUE) puts it back for a talk.
p_dev <- plot_by_age(d, "similarity", "similarity to adults (r)")
p_dev
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-consistency
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.2
# Deliberately the twin of fig-development: same function, same scales, same
# colours. Side by side the contrast is the finding - the similarity lines
# rise together, the consistency line for emotions does not.
p_con <- plot_by_age(d, "consistency", "test-retest consistency (r)")
p_con
```

```{r}
#| label: linearity
# The models above are linear in age. An effective degrees of freedom near 1
# means that is adequate; much above 1 means a straight line is averaging over
# real curvature.
d %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(out = map(data, ~ tibble(
    n = nrow(.x),
    gam_edf = round(summary(gam(similarity ~ s(age, k = 5), data = .x,
                                method = "REML"))$s.table[1, "edf"], 2),
    quad_p = signif(anova(lm(similarity ~ age, .x),
                          lm(similarity ~ poly(age, 2), .x))$`Pr(>F)`[2], 3)))) %>%
  select(-data) %>% unnest(out) %>% ungroup() %>% show_all()
```

# Emotions

Emotions differs from the object domains on three things at once, which is
worth stating before any of its results are interpreted developmentally: six
concepts rather than twelve, lower consistency in children, and much weaker
agreement among adults about what the structure should be.

```{r}
#| label: emotions-context
d %>%
  mutate(category = as.character(category)) %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(child_consistency = round(mean(consistency, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(S$adult_agreement %>%
              mutate(category = as.character(category)) %>%
              select(category, adult_pairwise = pairwise, adult_loo = loo),
            by = "category") %>%
  left_join(S$adult_ref %>%
              transmute(category, n_pairs = lengths(ref)),
            by = "category") %>%
  mutate(category = fct_domain(category)) %>%
  arrange(category) %>% show_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: export-figs
# ggsave() with no `plot =` writes last_plot(), which is whatever was printed
# most recently - not necessarily the figure named in the filename. Always
# pass the object.
dir.create("figs", showWarnings = FALSE)

ggsave("figs/fig-development.png", p_dev, width = 15.5, height = 6.2, dpi = 300)
ggsave("figs/fig-consistency.png", p_con, width = 15.5, height = 6.2, dpi = 300)

png("figs/fig-pipeline.png", width = 15.38, height = 6.0, units = "in", res = 300)
draw_pipeline()
dev.off()

list.files("figs")
```
